findings.title: Doorway refusal at the threshold
findings.claim: The command to enter becomes a concrete threshold scene: entry meets a gate, while turning back leaves the commanded advance short of overcoming resistance.
findings.mechanism: The focus entry form contacts the gate and overcoming forms in 5:23; the focus backs and reversal forms contact the surrounding refusal sequence in 5:22-23. Their meeting converts the warning from an abstract instruction into a movement that can reach a threshold or reverse before crossing it.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see what the prohibited turning does inside this episode: it interrupts passage at the point where entry would have become possession of the promised advance.
findings.containment: This is a bounded 5:21-23 threshold reading. It keeps the ordinary command to enter and the warning against retreat intact, and it does not assert a surah-wide path system or a universal law from the gate scene.

epistemic.reason: The channel nomination and its six branch records are trusted and have exact focus or context carriers; the finding remains limited to their supplied pericope contact.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişi ya da şey dışarıdaki bir konum veya durumdan içerideki konum veya duruma geçer.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus imperative carries movement from outside into the commanded land.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The gate occurrence in 5:23 supplies a concrete threshold for that movement.
branch_activations.activation: The ordinary entry command meets the gate image, so entering is heard as crossing a defined threshold rather than merely approaching a destination.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The command's required act is a passage through resistance, the point at which the episode can move toward overcoming.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch is used for entry in this pericope; no broader meaning of the root or universal promise is claimed.

branch_activations.carrier: The 5:23 gate carries the entrance of a thing as a concrete doorway.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The focus imperative explicitly orders the addressed group to enter.
branch_activations.activation: The context doorway gives the focus verb an inspectable boundary: the commanded land is approached through an entrance whose crossing matters.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Entry becomes the decisive act at a doorway, so refusal can be pictured as a failure to cross the offered threshold.
branch_activations.boundary: The doorway is a supplied contextual image, not a claim that the focus word itself lexically means door.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeye yönelmeyi bırakıp sırtını dönerek ondan uzaklaşmayı belirtir.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: 5:22 makes entry conditional on the inhabitants leaving, while 5:23 places overcoming after entry.
branch_activations.activation: The back-turning form meets the opposed entry sequences, so retreat is the movement that abandons the threshold before the promised advance can occur.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Turning one's back is rendered as withdrawal from a specific passage under resistance, not only as an interior attitude.
branch_activations.boundary: The war-retreat facet is not expanded into a complete military narrative beyond the supplied verses.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Hareketin temel yönü, bir varlığın daha önce bulunduğu yere veya duruma geri gelmesidir.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The following replies repeat the entry action and place it in opposing conditional orders.
branch_activations.activation: Repeated entry in the context supplies the forward movement that the focus reversal would undo.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The prohibition governs a return from the very action that could carry the group across the threshold.
branch_activations.boundary: Only the direction of return is retained; no separate restoration or return-to-owner sense is asserted.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Etkilenen varlık, yöneldiği yol veya işten başka tarafa çevrilir.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The context supplies the inhabitants' demanded exit and the gate as the blocked or contested direction.

branch_activations.carrier: The 5:23 overcoming form carries force that prevails over resistance.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The doorway scene holds entry and overcoming in one movement, with refusal appearing at the point between them.
branch_activations.boundary: The supplied image supports the local threshold relation; it does not guarantee an outcome outside the cited episode.

findings.title: Assignment tested by resistance
findings.claim: The completed divine writing of the land can be read as an assigned responsibility whose reality is tested by resistance, after the people have been reminded of bestowed favor and kingship.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb carries binding determination, while 5:20 supplies bestowed favor and political capacity and 5:22 supplies coercive opposition. Their contact changes the written land from a picture of frictionless entitlement into an assignment exercised under the resistance named next.
findings.reader_payoff: The phrase about what God wrote for them becomes active in the surrounding episode: the assignment is connected to remembered enablement and is shown as costly when opposition appears.
findings.containment: The ordinary benefactive decree remains intact. This is a qualified HFT-based contextual relation, and the live alternative that 5:20 functions as encouragement by status alone remains open; no universal theory of entitlement is claimed.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace has complete supplied coordinates and a focus return, but three contextual branch records are unresolved and the reader identity is legacy_unbound; those parts are therefore attributed rather than treated as verified lexicon.

findings.title: Entry before control of the outcome
findings.claim: The replies around the focus imperative expose two causal sequences: one postpones entry until the inhabitants leave, while the other places entry through the gate before overcoming; in this local exchange, committed passage precedes control of the result.
findings.mechanism: The focus entry form is repeated in 5:22 and 5:23, where the refusers attach it to an until-condition and the two men place it before victory. The gate, outward movement, overcoming, and reliance carriers make the order of acts visible rather than leaving entry as a result that waits for safety.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus command can be seen as the disputed first act: the question is whether conditions must become safe before entry or whether passage is the act through which the situation can change.
findings.containment: The finding preserves the ordinary historical exchange and is limited to its supplied pericope. The HFT reader inference treats the ordering as a causal model, while the live alternative that 5:23 is battle-specific encouragement remains visible.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace is strong and coordinate-complete, but its contextual branches lack registered lexicon descriptors and its reader identity is legacy_unbound; unresolved roles remain explicitly attributed.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: Entry is heard as the threshold act through which the promised change may become possible, rather than as arrival after the change is complete.

findings.title: Destination converted into wandering
findings.claim: The land first presented as a bounded, sanctified destination returns in the aftermath as the very ground of prolonged wandering, so turning back converts arrival into unarrival measured through time and loss.
findings.mechanism: The focus earth, sanctified-place, turning, and loss carriers contact 5:24's fixed sitting and 5:26's prohibition, forty-year duration, and wandering on the land. The same ground therefore changes function from destination to medium of circulation without arrival.
findings.reader_payoff: The final loss becomes larger than missing territory: the reader can see orientation and time entering the consequence while the same land remains underfoot.
findings.containment: The focus warning and ordinary land reference remain recoverable. This is a qualified HFT application of the supplied aftermath; the alternative that 5:26 is only an externally imposed penalty remains open, and no independent doctrine of punishment is added.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace has complete focus and context coordinates and exact focus returns, while several contextual branches are unresolved and the reader identity is legacy_unbound.

findings.title: Exploratory loss of enrolled standing
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the focus inscription, prohibited reversal, and loss can be pictured as a stripping from the divinely inscribed cohort, so territorial loss also becomes loss of enrolled standing.
findings.mechanism: The focus writing, reversal, and loss carriers contact the separation and exit roles attributed to 5:25. Registration supplies the social image, reversal supplies exposure, and separation supplies the movement out of a containing order; together they form a bounded social-material model of de-enrollment.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus loss can be perceived as a change in belonging as well as access: the group that was written for the land is imagined as losing its place within the assigned cohort when it turns away.
findings.containment: This remains exploratory and does not replace the ordinary territorial warning. The unresolved HFT branches provide roles only, not lexical glosses; the model is not the lexical meaning of reversal or transgression, and no definitive social status is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The HFT outlier supplies exact focus and 5:25 coordinates and an explicit containment warning, but its contextual branch registry is unresolved and its reader identity is legacy_unbound.
